You haven't been hacked. AOL IS Yahoo, that is, Yahoo hosts AOL's email service. Yahoo requires the use if OAuth2 for authentication. It looks like you are already set up for that, but please confirm your Incoming and SMTP server settings to make sure.

OAuth2 will require you to enter your credentials on a new device, and program or operating system updates might be seen as "new" devices. Until you do so you won't be able to send or receive.

In order for OAuth2 to work, you Thunderbird must be set to allow cookies, so please check that (the setting is found at <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Accept cookies from sites>.)

Step 1: Verify the account typeBefore we proceed, please double-check to make sure you are indeed using an IMAP account.

Step 2: Rebuild the global databaseSince the entire index is corrupted, we can try deleting the global database. Rebuilding this data will allow Thunderbird to generate fresh, clean records.

In Thunderbird, go to the menu and click Help > Troubleshooting Information.

Under Application Basics, look for the Profile Folder and open it.Close Thunderbird completely, but leave the opened folder visible on your screen.

In this folder, look for the file named global-messages-db.sqlite.Right-click the file and select Delete.


(Note: This file will not disappear permanently; it will automatically rebuild itself after restarting and will not damage your email data).

Restart Thunderbird.
